We import all blocks just fine, but the block created from the genesis file does not have the hash which is pointed to by the first blocks' `parentHash`. I believe this is because the supplied genesis has: ``` ... [27cf5c8a] "londonBlock": 0, [27cf5c8a] "arrowGlacierBlock": 0, [27cf5c8a] "grayGlacierBlock": 0, [27cf5c8a] "mergeNetsplitBlock": 0, [27cf5c8a] "shanghaiTime": 0, [27cf5c8a] "cancunTime": 0, [27cf5c8a] "pragueTime": 0, [27cf5c8a] "terminalTotalDifficulty": 131072, [27cf5c8a] "depositContractAddress": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", [27cf5c8a] "ethash": {} [27cf5c8a] }, ``` (So the genesis block is a Prague block) The original genesis file (that is: the file before being passed to `jq`) also has: ``` [27cf5c8a] "excessBlobGas": null, [27cf5c8a] "blobGasUsed": null ``` So this does not seem correct to me, for a Prague genesis (or: a Cancun genesis) we should want that those fields are present and set, right? Ok, nvm, just checked on hive2 https://hivetests2.ethdevops.io/suite.html?suiteid=1737473064-9e2ade400af4bc95185d02c24b7fe880.json&suitename=rpc-compat#test-33 Geth returns Prague blocks here, `"requestsHash":"0xe3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"` I think we might have a problem specifically in the genesis block import False alarm, just found a Prague-specific bug in our implementation 🙂 In our blockchain, specifically at the genesis handler, we used the sha256 hash of 0x000102 for the default (old version of requests hash), it should be sha256(). We can now run the tests 😄 Very nice!

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content:
<@194432762315407360> we are currently figuring out why EthJS immediately exits the client. The problem is the initial blockchain import. We import all blocks just fine, but the block created from the genesis file does not have the hash which is pointed to by the first blocks' `parentHash`. I believe this is because the supplied genesis has:

```
...
[27cf5c8a]     "londonBlock": 0,
[27cf5c8a]     "arrowGlacierBlock": 0,
[27cf5c8a]     "grayGlacierBlock": 0,
[27cf5c8a]     "mergeNetsplitBlock": 0,
[27cf5c8a]     "shanghaiTime": 0,
[27cf5c8a]     "cancunTime": 0,
[27cf5c8a]     "pragueTime": 0,
[27cf5c8a]     "terminalTotalDifficulty": 131072,
[27cf5c8a]     "depositContractAddress": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
[27cf5c8a]     "ethash": {}
[27cf5c8a]   },
```

(So the genesis block is a Prague block)

The original genesis file (that is: the file before being passed to `jq`) also has:

```
[27cf5c8a]   "excessBlobGas": null,
[27cf5c8a]   "blobGasUsed": null
```

So this does not seem correct to me, for a Prague genesis (or: a Cancun genesis) we should want that those fields are present and set, right?

I think when these tests were written, we were at a fork like London, but it seems like genesis files get auto-updated to include things which affect blocks like Blobs.
